newsitem.title: FRANCE: CCFA sees 97 French car market down 15.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: CCFA sees 97 French car market down 15.6 pct.

text.p: The French carmakers committee CCFA predicted on Tuesday a fall of 15.6 percent in 1997 French car sales over 1996, confirming a forecast made last week by PSA Peugeot Citroen chairman Jacques Calvet.

CCFA president Yves de Belabre, who predicted in April sales might fall by 10-11 percent, told a news conference he now sees French car registrations of 1.8 million in 1997 against 2.13 million in 1996.
For the first six months of 1997 car sales in France were down 23.7 percent at 784,559 units, CCFA statistics showed.
De Belabre also said the European car market (17 countries) was expected to increase by around 2.0 percent this year.
He said car sales were expected to be down slightly in Germany but to rise by some five percent in Britain and some 10 percent in Spain.
In Italy sales were expected to jump some 30 percent thanks to a state rebate programme.
